title: Dharmendra Kumar Tripathi v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J. and Rajendra Kumar-IV, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; liberty to apply under Supply Code 2005 for consideration in accordance with law.
headnote: A writ seeking mandamus for a new or separate electricity connection to a partitioned ancestral house was disposed of without any opinion on merits. The petitioner was given liberty to apply within four weeks to the Chief Executive Engineer, KESKO, Kanpur Nagar, complying with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If so applied, the competent authority is to pass orders in accordance with law, preferably within the next four weeks.
facts: The petitioner sought a writ of mandamus directing the State and electricity authorities to provide a new or separate electricity connection to his partitioned ancestral house at 35/71, Bangali Mohal, Kanpur Nagar. Counsel for the petitioner and the standing counsel for respondents 1 and 2 were heard; none appeared for respondent 3. The standing counsel submitted that the petitioner could apply to respondent 3 for the connection, which would then be considered and decided in accordance with law.

holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the Court disposed of the writ with liberty to the petitioner to apply within four weeks to the Chief Executive Engineer, KESKO, Kanpur Nagar, for an electricity connection complying with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; on such an application, the competent authority shall pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, preferably within the next four weeks.

principle_tags.application: The Court refused mandamus for a new or separate connection and remitted the petitioner to apply to KESKO under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, for consideration in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner is entitled to a new or separate electricity connection on the partitioned ancestral premises
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits.
